title: Finite Stein base of a proper smooth generic curve
statement: Let $f:C\to S$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant morphism of excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] schemes, let $\eta$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of $S$, and suppose $C_\eta$ is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] irreducible curve of dimension $1$. There is a factorization $f=q\circ g$ through an excellent integral Noetherian scheme $S_0$, where $q:S_0\to S$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], dominant and projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and $g:C\to S_0$ is proper with geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] fibres. If $\eta_0$ is the generic point of $S_0$, then $\kappa(\eta_0)=H^0(C_\eta,\mathcal O_{C_\eta})$ is a finite separable extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] of $\kappa(\eta)$, and $C_{\eta_0}$ is a smooth geometrically integral curve of dimension $1$. Here $S_0=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(f_*\mathcal O_C)$ is the relative spectrum of the quasi-coherent algebra $f_*\mathcal O_C$; on an affine open $V\subset S$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_C)$.

source.place: Exposé IX, §1.3, printed p. 132, Stein-factorization paragraph; Stacks Tag 03H0 (more-morphisms-theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian), Tag 0BUG (varieties-lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections), Tag 0FD1 (varieties-lemma-baby-stein); Tag 0B3I (morphisms-lemma-finite-projective) for projective-bundle projectivity; Tag 07QU (more-algebra-lemma-finite-type-over-excellent) for excellence of finite type algebras.

proof.text: Form the relative spectrum S_0 = Spec_S(f_* O_C). Since f is proper over the Noetherian base and O_C is coherent, [lem-pc-coherent-hi] makes f_*O_C coherent (hence quasi-coherent), so the relative-spectrum construction applies. On an affine open V = Spec(A) of S, the restriction C_V -> V is proper and the relative-spectrum construction identifies S_0 x_S V with Spec Gamma(C_V,O_C). The canonical morphisms give C -> S_0 -> S and their composite is f. This is exactly the Stein factorization construction, with the affine descriptions and restriction compatibility supplied by the relative-spectrum node.

source.place: Exposé IX, §1.3, printed p. 132, Stein-factorization paragraph; Stacks 03GX and 01SA

proof.text: Fix an affine V = Spec(A) in S. Properness of C_V -> V and coherence of O_{C_V} give that Gamma(C_V,O_{C_V}) is a finite A-module by [lem-pc-coherent-hi]. Hence S_0 -> S is finite, since finiteness is affine-local on the target (by the relative-spectrum description of Step 1, q^{-1}(V) = Spec Gamma(C_V,O_C)). The same affine rings are domains: C_V is nonempty because f is dominant, and C is integral, so restriction of a section of O_C over the nonempty open C_V to the function field of C is injective. Integrality of S_0 and dominance of q are proved in Step 3. Since S is excellent and Noetherian, each finite (hence finite type) coordinate algebra Gamma(C_V,O_C) is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and S_0, being finite, hence of finite type, over the Noetherian S, is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Finally [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle] makes the finite map q projective in the required projective-bundle convention.

source.place: Exposé IX, §1.3, printed p. 132, finiteness and excellence of the Stein base; Stacks 03H0, 02O5 and 07QU

proof.text: On each affine V = Spec(A), apply the affine Stein-factorization theorem to C_V -> V. It says that the first map C_V -> Spec Gamma(C_V,O_C) is proper and that each of its fibres is geometrically connected, in particular nonempty. Since g^{-1}(q^{-1}V) = C_V and the restriction of g over q^{-1}V is this map, the fibre of g over a point of q^{-1}V is the fibre of C_V -> Spec Gamma(C_V,O_C), and properness is local on the target; so g:C -> S_0 is proper with geometrically connected fibres. Integrality of S_0: every fibre of g is nonempty, so g is surjective and S_0 = g(C) is irreducible as the continuous image of the irreducible C. S_0 is nonempty, and it is reduced because it is covered by the opens q^{-1}V = Spec Gamma(C_V,O_C) whose rings are domains by Step 2. Hence S_0 is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, i.e. integral by the equivalent characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Dominance of q: f = q o g is dominant, so the image of q contains the dense set f(C).

source.place: Exposé IX, §1.3, printed p. 132, Stein-factorization paragraph; Stacks 03H2 (1), (3)

proof.text: Let K = kappa(eta). The generic fibre C_eta is the base change of the proper morphism f, hence proper; it is integral because affine charts of the dominant morphism from the integral C are obtained by localizing domains, and it is a smooth curve by hypothesis. Therefore [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] says that L := H^0(C_eta,O_{C_eta}) is a finite field extension of K. Smoothness gives geometric reducedness by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], so [lem-pc-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections-separable] makes L/K separable. The relative-spectrum restriction and [lem-sc-fraction-field-sections-base-change] identify the generic relative-spectrum algebra with Gamma(C_eta,O_C_eta)=L; since S_0 is integral and finite dominant over S, its generic point eta_0 has residue field L. Thus kappa(eta_0)=L and the displayed finite separable extension is the claimed one.

source.place: Exposé IX, §1.3, printed p. 132, identification of the Stein generic field; Stacks 0BUG and 0FD1

proof.text: The Stein fibre is C_{eta_0}=C\times_{S_0}Spec(L). It is canonically isomorphic to C_eta: indeed S_0\times_S Spec(K) is Spec(L) (Step 4), with Spec(L) -> S_0 the inclusion of the generic point eta_0, and associativity of fibre products identifies C\times_{S_0}(S_0\times_S Spec(K)) with C\times_S Spec(K). Under this identification the L-structure of C_eta is the canonical map C_eta -> Spec Gamma(C_eta,O_{C_eta}) = Spec(L). This is not the generally larger scheme C_eta\times_{Spec(K)}Spec(L). C_{eta_0} -> Spec(L) is proper, being the base change of the proper g ([lem-pc-proper-base-change](1)); so it is separated and of finite type. To prove smoothness over Spec(L), let W=C_eta\times_{Spec(K)}Spec(L). The extension L/K is finite and separable (Step 4); for an algebraic extension the empty set is a transcendence basis, so separability in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] means L/K is separable algebraic, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] makes Spec(L) -> Spec(K) etale. The projection W -> C_eta is its base change, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. It is separated: over an affine open Spec(R) of C_eta it is Spec(R\otimes_K L) -> Spec(R), a morphism of affine schemes, whose diagonal is the closed immersion given by the surjective multiplication map, and separatedness is local on the target. The graph of the structure map C_eta -> Spec(L) is a section of W -> C_eta, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] makes it an isomorphism of C_eta onto a clopen subscheme of W; composed with the second projection W -> Spec(L) this section is the structure map C_eta -> Spec(L). By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), W -> Spec(L) is smooth (base change of the smooth C_eta -> Spec(K)), and its restriction to the open subscheme C_eta is smooth, smoothness being local on the source. The affine Stein theorem [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine](iii) gives geometric connectedness of this fibre over L. After any field extension Omega/L, the base change C_{eta_0,Omega} is smooth over Omega by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), of finite type over the field Omega hence locally Noetherian, and its local rings are local rings of smooth Omega-algebras on affine opens, hence regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]; it is nonempty and connected by geometric connectedness. Applying [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] to this nonempty connected regular scheme shows it is integral, so C_{eta_0} is geometrically integral over L. Finally C_{eta_0} is isomorphic as a scheme to C_eta, which has dimension one by hypothesis, so C_{eta_0} has dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; hence it is a smooth geometrically integral curve of dimension one over L.

split_report.summary: Split the finite Stein-base lemma into five source-driven steps. The relative spectrum and affine Stein theorem provide the factorization, finiteness, properness and geometrically connected fibres; coherent cohomology makes the affine Stein algebras finite, and the new statement-only child lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle supplies the required projective-bundle projectivity of a finite morphism. The generic fibre is handled by proper smooth base change, finite global sections, and separability of global sections of a proper geometrically reduced scheme; smooth geometrically connected field fibres are shown geometrically integral using regularity and connectedness. No statement change was made.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Stein-factorization paragraph of the ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality used in the alteration branch.

The statement is unchanged and no node is dropped.
